summary:
Wrote `plan.md`: all four modules share one column section. Fluted quartz-pillar Doric columns, spaced 8 apart, stand 4 blocks in front of a recessed diorite wall of tall windows, over a rusticated base, with a triglyph entablature, attic and balustrade. The portico and corner pavilion stand 1 block forward, and wing bays tile with no visible seam.
The portico carries six columns plus flanking pairs, three arched doorways reached by slab steps, and a pediment with relief.
Plot 0 sets a 46-across drum (16 paired columns, 8 tall windows, stepped attic) on the square pavilion. On it goes a lead-grey tuff dome with 16 andesite ribs and a gold band, then a columned lantern and gold cupola and finial to y 125. Gold appears only there, so the gilded dome over the colonnade is what makes it read as City Hall. Nothing was built or rendered, so none of this has been checked yet. A Beaux-Arts palace in four modules sharing one wing section: a rusticated diorite base, giant 2x2 quartz_pillar Doric columns standing 4 in front of a recessed wall of tall grey-glass windows, a triglyph entablature, an attic and a diorite balustrade, the pattern tiling seamlessly on a 4-block grid.
The portico adds three arched doorways with slab steps, six columns plus flanking pairs and a calcite pediment carrying quartz relief. The corner pavilion turns the corner on pilastered antas under a taller panelled attic.
Plot 0 stacks the same order on four faces, a drum ringed by 16 paired columns, a 2-thick polished_tuff dome (16 andesite ribs, gold band, ring and cartouches, glowstone in the inner shell), and a columned gold-cupola lantern to y 125. The design is written but not yet built or rendered.

front shell: Wrote parts/front-shell.mjs, which builds the masonry for plots 1–3. That covers the rusticated bases, terraces, recessed walls, entablatures, attics, decks, floors, rear and party walls, the portico's central attic block, and the plot 3 piers with plain south and west walls. make.sh gave 30278 blocks placed, with no refused writes and nothing off-palette. mcd check finds nothing floating, and the front-right render reads as a long granite front.
polish: I ticked P1 in plan.md but did not tick the elements.md items.
Columns, glass, triglyph cells, cornice cells, balustrades, the pediment zone and the door openings are left empty, as specified.
Plot 3 east: the window at z 6..7 is omitted, because the north window at x168..169 already owns the cell x169,z6. P9 should glaze the other two east windows at z 15..16 and 24..25.
The portico flank attics have no windows. The plan lists them at x79..80 and x111..112, but those cells fall inside the pediment span.
The plot 3 anta piers are solid polished_diorite from y 10 to 33, with no rustication joints above y 9.
The deck steps from y39 to y42 at plot 3's x144..146 strip, so there is a wall step at z7/8 that can only be seen from above.
I added y36 smooth_stone at x73..118, z7..11 to support the pediment's back; this is noted in plan.md.
I did not run mcd fit or the plot 2 tiling render test.

waste.what: Worked out by hand the u/d to x/z mapping for each module: window pairs across the plot joints (127, 135, 143), and the pier and corner overlaps on plot 3.
waste.cost: about 40 minutes of reasoning, several overlapping cells, and one lost heredoc write.
waste.tool: A facade-spec helper, e.g. `frontBay({plane, windows, tall, doors, plain})`, that runs rusticatedBase, recessedWall, entablature, attic and the keystone back-fill in one call. A `joints` option to complete half-windows across plots would help too.

waste.what: I wrote fill-based floors, party walls and piers by hand, because the vocab has no helper for solid blocks.
waste.cost: about 15 fill calls.
waste.tool: `floors(g, box, levels)` and `partyWall` helpers.

companions.task: Rusticated anta piers and the joints on the piers above y 9
Check the window cells across plot joints and at plot 3's NE corner, where the north and east windows compete for x169,z6

summary:
dome pavilion shell: P2 built in parts/pavilion-shell.mjs: plot 0's square pavilion (base, terrace, recessed wall, entablature ring on all four faces), 3x3 rusticated corner piers, plinth corners, y1 rotunda floor and the y36 deck with the r18.5 hole.
make.sh ran clean: 22432 blocks placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette, check shows no floating blocks, fit OK.
E and W faces carry five windows (no 7..8 or 55..56, which sat on the N/S corners); N and S carry seven. plan.md's Notes record this for P9.
polish: P4 must place the triglyphs (y35, d2), the d1 cornice ring at y36 and the y37..38 balustrade, plus the base sills and keystones for plot 0's windows (keystone cells at d2, y8 are left air for it).
P9 glazing: plot 0 windows are N/S at u 7,15,23,31,39,47,55 and E/W at 15,23,31,39,47 (the plan's OPENINGS list 7..8 and 55..56 on every face; those are not open on E/W).

Columns (P3) at d2..3 y10..33 and the drum/dome/lantern (P6-P8) are not built here; the deck over the rotunda is x/z 8..55 because the y36 ring is the entablature crown, not x/z 2..61 as the plan's table reads.
elements.md items 10, 14, 28 and 29 are only partly built and are marked [~] with the reason.

waste.what: Worked out the corner partition by hand: which face owns each corner cell of the ring (plinth L's, pier outer rings, entablature/terrace/recessed-wall overlaps), and which windows fall on a corner.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reasoning, several overlap cases checked on paper before any code ran
waste.tool: a faceRing/partition helper in the vocabulary (for example faceFrame with a corner policy: N/S own the corners, E/W take the strip between, emitting each face's u-range for each helper) would have made this a one-liner; a plan table of per-face u-ranges per element would also do it.

waste.what: Hand-wrote the corner pier and plinth L-shapes as box() calls and a pier joint rule (outer ring air at y4/y7, next ring diorite).
waste.cost: about 12 fills and one 3x3 loop; no retries
waste.tool: a vocab pierBlock(g, x0, z0, y0, y1, {joints, outer}) helper that does the rusticated 3x3 corner with base joints.

waste.what: Checked the plot 0 faces by reading the full-site render and the zoom tiles; the whole-site front-left render is too small to judge a single plot.
waste.cost: three renders, two of them zoomed by eye
waste.tool: mcd render --plot x0,z0,x1,z1 (crop to one plot at a readable scale) would have shown the pavilion alone.

companions.task: Lay the corner piers' rustication joints and the y1 base course behind the plinth, and check the joints match the base faces block for block.
Fit the plot 0 windows on the E and W faces, deciding whether the corner windows at 7..8 and 55..56 can be fitted at all, and set the connection states along the wall.
Place the triglyphs, the d1 cornice ring and the y37..38 balustrade on the four faces, against the entablature gaps I left at y35 d2.

summary:
giant order: parts/giant-order.mjs builds all 40 giant columns (y 10..33: plot 0 24, plot 1 10, plot 2 2, plot 3 4) and the four plot-3 anta pilasters (north x147..149 and 172..174 at z0, east z1..3 and 28..30 at x175).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt: 4128 blocks placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Counts match the plan (40 x 96 + 4 x 72 = 4128).
The columns sit on the plan's footprints; plot 0 columns float until the pavilion shell (P2) supplies its terrace and walls. mcd fit showed nothing for my cells.
polish: Plot 0's 24 columns report as FLOATING in mcd check (2304 blocks): they stand on no terrace yet, because the pavilion shell (P2) is still a stub. They should be supported once P2 lands; re-check then.
Element 28 (plot 0 giant order on all four faces) is only the columns; the wing section, rusticated piers and windows around them are P2's.
Element 24 (corner pavilion) is only the pilasters and the north/east column pairs; the pavilion block itself is P1's.

The render was checked at tile size only (front-left iso and the 300 px elevation); the columns read as a ring on plot 0 and as the portico rhythm, but no close-up was made. A zoom on the portico and the pavilion's east face would confirm the column pair spacing.

waste.what: Worked out every column footprint by hand from the plan's tables (40 x/z pairs across four plots and both sides of the dome) and wrote one doricColumn call per column.
waste.cost: about 40 coordinate pairs computed by hand; one pass, no retries
waste.tool: A plan-driven column placer: a table in plan.md (or plan.json) of {plot, face, u, d} rows, read by a helper that calls doricColumn and antaPilaster, so a part lists positions once and the rhythm is checked against the plan's face frames.

waste.what: Confirmed column counts and pilaster cells by reading the census and the placed count, not by a per-face check.
waste.cost: a few mental multiplications (40 x 96, 4 x 72) and one check of the census (3520 quartz_pillar = 40 x 22 x 4)
waste.tool: `mcd info` or a make.sh line that reports placed blocks per named sub-group (e.g. per plot and face), so a worker sees a wrong count at once.

waste.what: Viewed the build as small render tiles (300 px elevation and a 420 px iso); too small to check column pair spacing, so I relied on the coordinates.
waste.cost: two renders, no zoom
waste.tool: `mcd zoom` at each column pair on a face (the toolkit already has it) run as a standard step, with a per-part close-up list in the kit.

companions.task: Lay the plot 0 pavilion walls and the rusticated base so the 24 dome-pavilion columns stand on a terrace instead of floating, and check the corner piers against the column spacing.
Cut the portico's flanking-pair capitals and the pediment's raking cornice to meet the giant columns' tops at y 33 and y 34.

summary:
stone dressings: P4 stone dressings built in parts/dressings.mjs: triglyphs, cornices (y36), balustrades, base-window sills and keystones, upper sills, and the plot 3 attic panels, 1560 blocks, 0 refused, all on palette.
make.sh runs clean and leaves a whole build.nbt; the zooms of the wing, pavilion east face and dome corner read as cornice, triglyph frieze and balustrade.
Plan.md's P4 box is ticked and elements 4, 8, 10, 13 and 25 are marked; the floating dome-plinth and entablature cells are P2's, not yet built.
polish: Outer corner stairs are not set: the north and west cornice runs meet at the dome corners and the pavilion's NE corner as straight stairs. The zoom reads acceptably, but a stair joiner should check for a true outer-corner shape.

Plot 3 west strip (x 144..146): I added the wing cornice (z1), triglyphs (z2) and balustrade (z3, y40). These depend on P1 building the attic at y 37..41 there, and on a plinth at z1 for the joint sills at x 143..144, which I did not verify.
The single joint sill at x 64 has only its terrace (y10) slab. I dropped the top slab because it was an orphan, so the joint column has no y22 sill.
The 8 floating-cell groups in the check are all P2's: the dome-pavilion plinth and entablature the cornices and balustrades sit on, plus the plot 0 base sills at x 1 / x 62. They clear once P2 lands.
I did not run `mcd fit` or `mcd approach`; P4 has no doors or shutters, so no approach to check.

waste.what: Each face's cornice, balustrade and triglyph run was called by hand with its own u-range, depth and corner exclusions (four dome faces, the portico in three depth runs, the pavilion's north and east), worked out cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 40 helper calls and 3 corner-exclusion decisions, written and re-checked by hand
waste.tool: A `faceRun(g, face, box, {cornice|balustrade|triglyphs}, ...)` in the vocabulary that splits a plot's ring into runs and takes the corners once (outer-corner shape set automatically). `mcd plan` could also list each plot's depth runs from plan.md tables.

waste.what: Base-window dressing and upper sills were called window by window from the OPENINGS table (7 windows per dome face, 3 per pavilion face, the joint pairs), with the tall central portico openings and the single joint column picked out by hand.
waste.cost: about 30 window calls and 6 manual single-cell slabs, plus one orphan found and removed by a rebuild
waste.tool: A `dressOpenings(g, F, openings)` helper that reads the plan's OPENINGS rows (glass depth, tall or two-storey, joint half) and emits sills, keystones and tall-window sills from them in one call.

waste.what: I verified the corners and the east face by eye from zoom renders, one render per check, instead of a measured corner-shape check.
waste.cost: 3 zoom renders and 2 rebuilds
waste.tool: `mcd zoom` at a corner with an outer-corner stair check, or `mcd check --corners` to report the stair shape at each corner cell.

companions.task: Cut the triglyph frieze, the keystones over the base windows and the acroteria-style joints, and set the outer-corner cornice stairs where the dome's north and west runs and the pavilion's north and east runs meet.
Build the outer-corner cornice stairs (outer_left/outer_right shapes) at the four dome corners and the pavilion's NE corner, and check each cornice run's ends against the wall it returns into.

summary:
portico front: Portico front built in parts/portico.mjs: three arched doorways (doors, transoms, haunches, voussoirs, keystones) on the east-front base, the raking pediment with tuff roof, ridge, acroteria, and the relief at z 1.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the portico line reads 3210 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. mcd check reports no floating or unsupported blocks, and mcd fit reports OK.
Render of the pediment and doors reads as the plan intends. The street approach passes on a +1 z-shifted copy (4 cells, rise 1); on the kit alone it cannot run because z -1 is outside the structure.
polish: mcd approach from the real street cell 95,1,-1 cannot run on the kit alone (z starts at 0); verified on a copy shifted +1 in z, so the placement must keep the street row at z -1 in the same frame.
The relief figures in the pediment read as crude pillars and blocks, not as figures; a carver could refine them later.
elements.md has no tick column, so elements 16-22 are ticked only in plan.md Notes.

waste.what: Shifted the whole structure by +1 in z in a scratch copy just to run mcd approach from the street cell.
waste.cost: one node script, one extra approach run; about 2 minutes
waste.tool: mcd approach should take an offset or a --street-ground option so a street cell outside the kit (z -1) can be checked without a shifted copy.

waste.what: Rebuilt after passing the plot object where faceFrame expects an array, and used sed -i (BSD sed) with a pattern that failed; both were manual retries.
waste.cost: two failed make runs and one failed sed
waste.tool: faceFrame could accept the PLOTS entry directly, or the plot constant could be exported as an array; a note in the vocab about the array form would have saved the retry.

waste.what: Read the pediment close-up in a separate render because the default portico view cropped the roof.
waste.cost: one extra render call
waste.tool: mcd render --closeups with a pediment or gable close-up would have shown the roof without a custom --view.

companions.task: Refine the pediment relief: the seated and reclining figures (plan rule 23) read as pillars and blocks, so a carver would shape the heads, drapery and figure silhouettes within the same cells.
Check the three transom glass panes and the door reveals over each arch in a close-up render, and confirm the glass connection states agree with the glazing part's panes.

summary:
drum: parts/drum.mjs builds the drum on plot 0, y 37..70: stylobate and inner ledge, drum wall, 16 paired giant columns, 8 glazed drum windows, entablature with inward cornice stairs, stepped attic with 8 small windows at y 66, 8 urns and the top step.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; the drum reports 11660 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette, and `mcd fit` is OK.
Zoomed renders from north and east read as a columned drum with windows, cornice and urns. Its support was checked on a stand-in y 36 deck; the real deck is P2's.
polish: The drum floats in the assembled build until P2 lays the plot 0 deck at y 36 (deck r > 18.5); on a stand-in deck it is fully supported.
Inner ledge is ringFill(18.5, 19.5] at y 37..40, not 17.5..19.5: the deck hole at r <= 18.5 would leave 17.5..18.5 hanging. Recorded in plan.md Notes.
Attic and drum window glass (y 66 and y 44..57) is placed by this part, so P9 must not also glaze the drum. The spec's ambiguity here is resolved that way.
Ring cornice stairs at y 64 face the dominant compass axis toward the centre, with no outer-corner shapes; corners may look slightly stepped.

Support fixes beyond the spec: the outer sill sits on a y 41..42 plinth, the inner sill is a top slab, the y 58 head has a lintel course, y 59..60 are wall over the inner cells, and the hood's centre at y 59 is a full block. Recorded in plan.md Notes.
Lanterns on the drum ledge (y 41, P10) need the ledge top at y 40, which is smooth_quartz. Not verified against mcd light yet.

waste.what: Worked out the 16 column corners, 8 window axes and 8 urn angles by hand from the plan table, and wrote the ring and band geometry again beside drumWindow's own internal band logic.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reading plus one rewrite of the band test
waste.tool: A vocab export such as drumWindowCells(cx, cz, angleDeg, width) that returns the band, glass, sill and head cells, and a plan.json entry for the column table that the part can import.

waste.what: Found the unsupported cells by building, then running `mcd fit`, then rebuilding. The sill, hood and head each needed a fix that drumWindow does not make.
waste.cost: 3 build/fit cycles
waste.tool: drumWindow option supported:true (plinth under the outer sill, lintel course at the head, full-block hood centre), or a fit check that names the helper and the missing support.

waste.what: Checked the drum's support by writing a scratch script that puts a stand-in deck under it, because `mcd check` on a part alone reports every block as floating.
waste.cost: one scratch script and one extra check run
waste.tool: `mcd check --assume-ground y36` or a per-part check that treats the rest of the plan's deck as present.

waste.what: Chose each urn cell by searching the ring for the nearest angle, and checked the 45° and 22.5° geometry by hand.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of coordinate reasoning
waste.tool: A ringCellAt(cx, cz, rIn, rOut, angleDeg) helper in vocab/h3.

companions.task: Lay the drum's stylobate, the 16 paired columns' feet and fluting, and the entablature with the cornice stairs, so the ring-curved stair facings are cut properly rather than as the dominant-axis approximation.
Set the ring cornice at y 64 and the window heads at y 58, with their inward facings and outer-corner shapes where the ring turns.
Light the drum's ledge at y 41 and the attic step, and confirm with `mcd light --y 41` that no walkable cell on the ledge is dark.

summary:
dome: P7 dome is built in parts/dome.mjs: leadDome puts the leaded polished_tuff shell (y 71..100, r 20.5) with a gold band at y 71, 16 polished_andesite ribs, gold cartouches at y 73, a gold ring at y 100 and glowstone on rings y 74..98.
The dome's top is closed under the lantern: the y 100 disc inside r 5.5 is solid (88/88), so the y 101 platform has solid support.
make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt; the dome line shows 6560 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. The render shows the ribs as pale lines on the grey.
polish: The dome sits on the drum's top course at y 70, which is still a stub in this copy: `mcd check` reports 6560 floating blocks until P6 lands. Nothing in the dome part needs changing for that.

The gold ring at y 100 covers most of the lantern disc (68 of 88 cells are gold), so the top reads as a gold cap rather than a grey shell with a gold rim. That follows the spec's ring rule; say if the top should be grey.

waste.what: Checking the dome layer by layer (shell, ribs, gold, glow, lantern-disc closure) with a hand-written scan script over the built nbt.
waste.cost: one scratch script, two runs; about 4 minutes
waste.tool: A `mcd layers build.nbt --y-range 70,102 --census` (per-y block counts, optionally restricted to a centre and radius) would have answered this in one command.

waste.what: Closing the y 100 lantern disc by hand: scanning the r<=5.5 cells for air and writing polished_tuff into each one.
waste.cost: one extra loop in parts/dome.mjs; 20 air cells found by a scan
waste.tool: leadDome could take a `closeTop: {r, y}` option so the closure is built in the dome brush itself, not patched after it; the vocabulary would also need that rule in its spec.

waste.what: Verifying that the lantern disc is closed (88/88 at y 100) with a separate check script.
waste.cost: one scratch script
waste.tool: `mcd check --at x,y,z --radius r` or a 'solid disc' assertion in the vocabulary tests would have caught the gap automatically.

companions.task: Check the dome's lead-coloured shell and the stair edges against the concept photo: is the polished_tuff/polished_andesite rib contrast right, and do the stair edges round off the outline at the base?
Decide the gold ring and cartouche arrangement at y 73 and y 100 (cells of the gold ring that stick out vs the disc), and where a gold cap should stop so the lantern base is not swamped in gold.
Build the drum (y 37..70) under the dome; the dome currently floats until it lands on the drum's top course at y 70.

summary:
lantern: P8 lantern is built: parts/lantern.mjs calls lanternTemple(g, 31.5, 31.5, 101), giving the smooth_quartz platform, eight quartz_pillar posts with gold capitals, the glass ring, the entablature and gold band, the gilded cupola (dome r3.5), the gold finial with a quartz collar and four lightning rods, and two hanging lanterns under the y109 ceiling.
make.sh saved a whole build.nbt: the lantern line shows 842 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. A close-up zoom reads as a columned lantern with a gold cupola and finial.
plan.md's P8 box is ticked; the lantern's elements 38, 39 and 41 are built.
polish: Standalone, the 842 lantern blocks float (check: 1 floating group, y 101..125). They rest on the dome crown at y 100, which the dome part (P7) must build with the r<=5.5 disc closed.

Light on the temple floor (y 102) is min 2, mean 5.6, dim 44 of 52 cells; no cell is at 0, so mobs cannot spawn there, but it is below the 8+ target. I kept the plan's two hanging lanterns at (31,108,31) and (32,108,32) rather than adding lamps; the platform sits above the dome and is not walkable. Say if you want more lamps.
elements.md has no tick column, so the 38/39/41 items are not ticked there; only plan.md's P8 box was ticked.

waste.what: Cross-checked each plan coordinate (posts, glass ring radii, y-levels 101..125, cupola centre, finial cells) against vocab/h3.mjs lanternTemple by reading its source, to confirm the helper matched the plan rather than trusting the summary.
waste.cost: about 5 minutes of reading and arithmetic; no blocks placed by hand
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for vocab helpers (for example mcd plan-cells lanternTemple --at 31.5,31.5,101) that prints each element's footprint as box and y-range, checkable against plan.md without reading the source.

waste.what: Checked the temple's light by reading the map rows for y 102 and counting dim cells by eye; the rows show the lantern as a symmetric 9 falling off to 2 at the rim.
waste.cost: one mcd light call and manual reading of about 40 rows
waste.tool: mcd light --summary-only, or a mode that reports the light at the lit spots and the worst cell's position for a lantern group.

waste.what: The shipped build has no roof or dome under the lantern, so the structure check reports every lantern block as floating. Checking my part in isolation meant reading past that noise by hand.
waste.cost: one mcd check run plus manual filtering of the FLOATING line
waste.tool: mcd check --ignore-floating-below y (or a per-part mode that treats the unbuilt neighbour as supported) so a part can be checked alone.

companions.task: Decide whether the crown's temple floor (y 102) needs lamps beyond the two hanging lanterns the plan gives, given min 2 and the 8+ target, and check that the outer ring is not a spawn gap once the dome is built.
Judge the gold cupola and finial proportions from the street view, and check that the gold band at y 111 and the cupola's gold read as one gilding, not stacked blocks.

summary: glazing: ["parts/glazing.mjs glazes every OPENINGS window on plots 0-3 (1784 gray_stained_glass_pane) at each opening's glass depth, via glassRun through the face frames; drum, lantern and door transoms are not glazed.", "connectPanes joins each pane to any glass neighbour, so corner cells shared by two plot 0 faces connect round the corner; make.sh finishes with no refusals and no off-palette blocks.", "plan.md: P9 ticked and a P9 note added. The build's plot 0 glass and some joint panes float until P2 closes walls and P1/P2 fill the gaps they own."]
polish: Plot 0's glass floats until P2 closes the pavilion walls (the check shows 8 floating glass groups there); this is expected in this run because P2 is still a stub.

Pane connections: the joint columns at x 64 and x 144 set their outer side to connect, but the neighbour there is air until P2 builds plot 0's east/west walls, so a small arm may stick out. Visual check needed once the parts merge.
Plan mismatch: OPENINGS puts the central attic glass at z 12, but the attic helper puts it one in, at z 13 (the open cell is z 12). I used z 13.
Plan mismatch: the portico flank attic windows at x 79..80 and 111..112 (y 38, z 3) sit inside the pediment's solid tympanum, so they are not built. P1 also notes the flank attics have no windows.
P1's east recessed wall gap at x 169..170, z 5..6, is P1's to close. I left the east upper z 6..7 window out, as P1's note says; its corner glass is the north window's x 169 z 6.
Only build.nbt, plan.md and my module were edited. The full build was not rendered at 1:1 because the other parts are still stubs; I looked at the front-left tile and one zoom of the wing bay.

waste.what: Hand-enumerated every window's u-range, glass depth and y-band per face (about 80 glassRun calls, with the plot 0 faces written out four times), and checked corner collisions by hand.
waste.cost: about 20 min of coordinate bookkeeping and 3 rebuild retries
waste.tool: An OPENINGS-driven helper, e.g. glazeOpenings(g, face, [{u0,u1,d,y0,y1}]) or a data table read straight from plan.md's OPENINGS, that also dedupes corner cells and sets pane connections.

waste.what: Corner-pane connection fix-up (a pane joins glass round a corner) and the check of which refusals are real: both done by reasoning, not by a tool.
waste.cost: 2 rebuilds to tell duplicate corner writes from real refusals
waste.tool: glassRun should report refusals by cause (already glass, solid, out of box) and set through-connections where a neighbour pane exists.

waste.what: Checking which window cells the front shell really opened, by reading its recessedWall and attic calls against the plan's tables and the P1 note.
waste.cost: about 10 min reading front-shell.mjs against plan OPENINGS
waste.tool: A `mcd openings check build.nbt --plan plan.md` that lists plan openings whose cells are not air, and which are still solid, so the gaps show up in one table rather than from a render.

companions.task: Fit the joint panes (x 127/128 and 143/144) and the corner panes at plot 0, and confirm the pane arms and connections read as one window with no seam.
Close P1's east recessed wall gap (x169..170, z 5..6) and decide the east upper window at z 6..7, since P1 omits it and P9 has only its corner glass.

summary:
lighting: P10 lighting is built in parts/lighting.mjs: 975 lantern and chain placements on the fronts, portico, wings and pavilion, with the 6-grid interiors hung on chains to about 3 blocks above each walking floor.
The dome side is coded but skipped until P2 (pavilion shell) and P6 (drum) land: 24 loggia lanterns on the y 10 terrace, 36 deck lanterns at y 37, 26 drum-ledge lanterns at y 41, 19 deck-hole lanterns at y 34.
make.sh runs whole and writes build.nbt. check shows 0 floating or unsupported, fit is OK, and the y 10 and upper-floor light maps have no dark floor cells.
polish: Dome-side lanterns (plot 0 loggia on the y 10 terrace, the y 37 deck ring, the y 41 drum ledge, the y 34 deck-hole ring) skip until P2 and P6 build their terrace, deck, drum wall and ledge; rerun make.sh then to place them.
The rotunda floor (y 2) reads dark once P2 lands; the room-1 lampStandards must light it, since the deck-hole lanterns hang 32 blocks above the floor.
Exterior cells (the street-level ground at the z 0 front and at x 175) read dark on the block-light map. The kit has no street lamps, so that needs a site lighting pass or a lamp-post part.
